title: The Last Echo Revisited
premise: Freya Eastwick investigates 'impossible' insurance claims in the decaying colony of Vantage Hollow, a settlement erased from corporate charts after its terraforming contract failed. When gravity across the entire system stutters for exactly nine seconds, Freya discovers the flicker was a side effect of a mass driver used to bury evidence of a corporate-ordered massacre that killed four thousand colonists—evidence her late sister helped create. Pursued by adjusters who rewrite reality as easily as claims, Freya teams up with disgraced archivist Sef Oduya and the massacre's sole surviving witness to rebuild the erased record from physical traces: bones, slag, and the nine seconds of gravitational echo itself. In the end, she broadcasts the reconstructed truth to every ship in the system at the cost of her own anonymity, trading her invisible life for justice—and discovering her sister's final message hidden inside the echo.
about_author: A. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former risk analyst who spent a decade auditing disaster claims in remote industrial settlements before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn, morally tangled science fiction about ordinary people who refuse to let institutions define what really happened.

chapters.title: Claims Adjusted
chapters.summary: Freya Eastwick, POV. Investigating a collapsed hab-dome claim in dying colony Vantage Hollow, she notices the structural report doesn't match the slag patterns. Establishes her meticulous, detached voice and the colony's quiet decay. Emotional beat: professional curiosity masking grief she won't name.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Gravity across the whole system flickers for exactly nine seconds; her instruments, unlike everyone else's, record it. The colony panics; the orbital authority calls it sensor drift. Emotional beat: the thrill of being the only one who saw the truth.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Basement
chapters.summary: Sef Oduya's POV. Disgraced corporate archivist Sef, hiding in Vantage Hollow, recognizes the flicker's signature as a mass-driver recoil. He seeks out Freya, the only investigator whose data survived. Emotional beat: two lonely professionals recognizing each other's obsessions.

chapters.title: Paper Graves
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Insurance records show four thousand colonists listed as 'relocated' eleven years ago—yet their policies were paid out on a single batch claim. Someone monetized their disappearance. Emotional beat: cold horror dressed in paperwork.

chapters.title: What My Sister Left
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya finds her sister Mara's old field kit in storage, containing an encrypted drive labeled with the flicker's exact timestamp. Mara, a terraforming engineer, died in the 'relocation.' Emotional beat: grief finally given a shape.

chapters.title: The Adjusters Arrive
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. A corporate claims-adjustment team lands, politely offering to 'consolidate' all local records. Sef recognizes their lead, Voss, as the man who ended his career. Emotional beat: the dread of being hunted by people with clipboards and kill orders.

chapters.title: Decryption and Denial
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Mara's drive partially unlocks, revealing survey footage of a settlement that officially never existed—and audio of evacuation orders that were never given. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning your family was complicit in covering up atrocity.

chapters.title: The Witness in the Ice
chapters.summary: Freya and Sef's alternating POV. They trace the drive's coordinates to a glacier crevasse and find Tomas Rell, the massacre's sole survivor, kept alive by a failing medical stasis unit. Emotional beat: fragile, disbelieving hope.

chapters.title: Tomas Testifies
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. In fragments, he recounts the night security forces sealed the lower habitat and flooded it. He survived in a maintenance shaft for nine days. Emotional beat: the unbearable weight of being the only memory left.

chapters.title: Voss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Voss offers Freya a lucrative position and full restoration of her sister's reputation—in exchange for the drive and Tomas. She realizes they know exactly who she is. Emotional beat: temptation measured against the dead.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The adjusters torch the colony's records office; Freya's official files are retroactively falsified, making her an unlicensed fraudster. The colony that ignored her now fears her. Emotional beat: the loneliness of erasure, mirrored.

chapters.title: Running on Empty Air
chapters.summary: Freya, Sef, and Tomas flee into the underlevels, pursued by adjusters. Tomas's stasis unit is failing; he has days. Freya must choose between finding a hospital and finding evidence. Emotional beat: love against duty, in miniature.

chapters.title: The Mass Driver
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They reach the abandoned mass driver that fired the burial load into the system's debris ring—and discover the flicker happens because the ring's mass is decaying, and in three weeks the buried evidence will drift into a public shipping lane. Emotional beat: the clock becomes visible.

chapters.title: What the Echo Keeps
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef realizes the nine-second gravity flicker isn't decay—it's a resonance pulse Mara rigged into the driver as a dead-man's alarm, repeating her hidden data every cycle. Mara planned her own posthumous testimony. Emotional beat: awe and heartbreak at a sister's foresight.

chapters.title: Colony of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. To decode the full pulse they need the colony's original gravity-grid schematics, held by the settlers who've spent eleven years pretending nothing happened. Freya must ask the people she investigated to trust her. Emotional beat: a community choosing, at last, to remember.

chapters.title: The Settlers' Ledger
chapters.summary: Multiple settlers' POV, braided. An old forewoman reveals the colonists have kept a handwritten ledger of every name the corporations erased—four thousand entries, kept in secret for a decade. Emotional beat: quiet, stubborn dignity.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Voss's team raids the settlement; Sef is captured buying time for the others. Under interrogation, he feeds Voss a false decode location. Emotional beat: sacrifice as an act of faith in other people.

chapters.title: The Ring Heist
chapters.summary: Freya and Tomas's POV. They take a jury-rigged shuttle into the debris ring to plant a relay that will amplify Mara's echo to every receiver in the system. Tomas's stasis unit dies mid-flight; he wakes fully, choosing to be present. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Interrogation and Turn
chapters.summary: Sef and Voss's alternating POV. Voss, shaken by Sef's calm, reveals he was the junior adjuster who processed the original massacre claim—and has been burying it ever since to survive. Sef offers him the one thing he can't refuse: a way to stop being complicit. Emotional beat: the enemy's humanity, and its limits.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds, Broadcast
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The next flicker comes; the relay fires, and every screen in the system displays Mara's data, Tomas's testimony, and the settlers' ledger. Voss's team stands down as their own corporate channels light up with warrants. Emotional beat: catharsis—the invisible made undeniable.

chapters.title: The Price of the Record
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Justice arrives as tribunals and headlines, but Freya's falsified record means she'll never work again; Tomas, finally free, chooses to stay and help rebuild Vantage Hollow. Freya and Sef, bound by what they carried, face an uncertain future together. Emotional beat: the cost of survival, paid willingly.

chapters.title: The Last Echo
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Weeks later, Freya decodes the final layer of Mara's pulse: a personal message—'You always checked the numbers, Freya. Check them for the ones who can't.' She opens a small investigator's office in the rebuilt colony, taking only cases no one else will file. Emotional beat: grief resolved into purpose; the echo becomes a voice.
